title: Days, weeks and reading a clock
objective: Count days and weeks on a calendar, jump weekdays forward with the 7-day cycle and read clock time to the hour and half hour.
explanation: A week is a repeating cycle of 7 weekday names: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Any question that moves a date forward or backward is settled by dividing the number of days by 7 and using only the remainder. A calendar month shows whole weeks plus a few spare days, which is why a fixed date lands on different weekdays in different months. A clock has a short hour hand and a long minute hand: the minute hand makes one full lap of 60 minutes per hour while the hour hand moves to the next hour mark.
analogy: Think of weekdays as seven seats on a rotating wheel. Whole turns (multiples of 7 days) bring you back to the same seat, so only the leftover days move you to a new seat.

workedExamples.title: Counting days between two dates
workedExamples.problem: How many days are there from 5 March to 21 March?
steps: A subtraction inside the same month gives the gap directly.

workedExamples.title: Weekday after 20 days
workedExamples.problem: Today is Saturday. Which weekday falls 20 days later?
steps: Two whole weeks bring us back to Saturday.
Move 6 seats forward: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday.

rule.title: Week cycle
rule.detail: There are exactly 7 days in a week; the weekday repeats every 7 days.

rule.title: Remainder rule
rule.detail: The weekday shifts by (number of days mod 7); both directions use the same idea.

rule.title: Weeks and leftover days
rule.detail: n days = floor(n/7) weeks plus n mod 7 leftover days.

rule.title: Clock face
rule.detail: The long hand counts minutes (one lap = 60 minutes); the short hand counts hours (one lap = 12 hours).

mistakes.fix: Only the remainder after dividing by 7 matters: 20 mod 7 = 6.

mistakes.mistake: Counting the first date itself when counting between dates.
mistakes.fix: From 5 to 21 March, the 5th itself is not counted: 21 - 5 = 16 days.

mistakes.mistake: Mixing up the hour hand and minute hand.
mistakes.fix: The hour hand is short and slow; the minute hand is long and makes a full lap every hour.

memoryTip: Whole weeks vanish, leftovers move the weekday; gaps inside a month are simple subtraction.

practice.prompt: How many days are there from 4 June to 30 June?
Today is Wednesday. Which weekday comes 10 days later?
practice.answer: Saturday. 10 mod 7 = 3; Wednesday plus 3 days is Saturday.

practice.prompt: Break 25 days into weeks and leftover days.
